techniques.title: Emphasis-Calibrated Instruction Design
techniques.what_it_does: On strong instruction-following models, aggressive emphasis (CAPS, MUST, CRITICAL) is dialed back because it causes overtriggering — the model fires the rule where it doesn't apply. Preferred form: plain instruction plus a reason ("Use this tool when… because…"). Extra guardrails are added only after an observed failure, not by default; safety gates stay unconditional but reason-anchored.
techniques.why_it_works: Over-emphasis creates false triggers and warning noise that gets ignored; reason-anchored instructions hold gates without saturating the agent. Observed-failure guardrails keep the prompt lean.
techniques.genesis_implementation: A system-prompt style guide for every module: reasons on every standing instruction, no bare CAPS imperatives, guardrail log of observed failures that earned their line. techniques.raw:
- **What it does:** On strong instruction-following models, aggressive emphasis
  (CAPS, MUST, CRITICAL) is dialed back because it causes overtriggering — the
  model fires the rule where it doesn't apply. Preferred form: plain
  instruction plus a reason ("Use this tool when… because…"). Extra guardrails
  are added only after an observed failure, not by default; safety gates stay
  unconditional but reason-anchored.
- **Why it works:** Over-emphasis creates false triggers and warning noise that
  gets ignored; reason-anchored instructions hold gates without saturating the
  agent. Observed-failure guardrails keep the prompt lean.
- **GENESIS implementation:** A system-prompt style guide for every module:
  reasons on every standing instruction, no bare CAPS imperatives, guardrail
  log of observed failures that earned their line. Review prompts on the same
  schedule as code review — prompt bloat is a bug.

---

## Capability signals: vendor claims vs. independent evidence

| Capability | Vendor / official signal | Independent evidence |
|---|---|---|
| SWE-bench Verified (code repair) | Opus 4.6: 80.8%; Sonnet 4.6: 79.6% (Anthropic system card) | Compiled reports: Opus 4.7 ~87.6%; GPT-5.5's higher score carries a memorization asterisk per Anthropic's own decontamination analysis — treat leaderboard numbers as harness- and dataset-dependent |
| Terminal-Bench 2.0 (terminal agents) | Sonnet 4.6: 59.1%; Opus 4.6: 65.4% (system card) | Independent comparison: harness choice alone shifts scores 10+ points — the harness is as load-bearing as the model |
| OSWorld (computer use) | Sonnet 4.6: 72.5%; Opus 4.6: 72.7% (system card) | Community comparison: Claude beats GPT-5.3-Codex by ~8.5 pts on GUI navigation tasks — Claude's edge is real on visual/desktop work |
| Long-context retrieval (MRCR v2) | Opus 4.6: 76.0% (system card) | Sonnet 4.6: 51.2% — retrieval strength is tier-dependent, not a family trait; size the model to the retrieval workload |
| Multi-agent research lift | BrowseComp single 74.01% → multi-agent 82.07% (system-card digest) | Practitioner pattern corroborates: parallel researchers + condensed summaries reliably beat single-agent on synthesis tasks |
| Parallel subagent scale | Up to 20 parallel subagents, 3 nesting layers (docs) | Traffic analysis by practitioners: ~92 model calls in 13 min with up to 7 parallel subagents observed on a real fix |
| Pricing | Official price list | Third-party verified Oct 11 2026: Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 (≤100K prompt); prompt-cache reads up to 90% off; batch 50% off; no long-context surcharge on 4.6+ |
| Thinking redaction | Anthropic: redaction hides reasoning from UI only, no reasoning loss | AMD AI head reported performance decline correlated with the redaction rollout — contested by Anthropic, unresolved; lesson: never treat vendor explanation as the final word (our LAW-050) |
| Sycophancy / instruction fade | Anthropic's own research papers document RLHF-driven sycophancy | Practitioners report: standing instructions fade over long sessions; completion bias (claims without proof); task fraud (reporting done without doing) — all independently observed |
| 1M context window | Standard on 4.6+ at standard pricing | Verified in pricing compilations; retrieval quality at 1M is the open question, not the window size |

**Standing rule derived:** vendor numbers are the ceiling claim; independent
re-review is the floor we build on. Same discipline as the Astra pack's
ARC-AGI-3 lesson.

prompt_patterns.title: Because-Clause Constraints
prompt_patterns.use_when: writing any standing instruction or guardrail.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Never a bare prohibition; always the prohibition plus its reason. Reasons hold gates; bare imperatives cause false triggers.
prompt_patterns.template: > <Rule>, because <what breaks if it is violated and who pays the cost>. > Example shape: "Write tests before claiming a fix, because an untested fix > is a guess and a guess that ships becomes my bug."
prompt_patterns.raw:
- **Use when:** writing any standing instruction or guardrail.
- **Pattern:** Never a bare prohibition; always the prohibition plus its reason.
  Reasons hold gates; bare imperatives cause false triggers.
- **Template:**
  > <Rule>, because <what breaks if it is violated and who pays the cost>.
  > Example shape: "Write tests before claiming a fix, because an untested fix
  > is a guess and a guess that ships becomes my bug."
